units.zh: 唐制，取士之科，多因隋舊，然其大要有三。
units.en: Tang rules for selecting officials drew heavily on Sui practice, but in essence there were three main paths.
units.literal: Under Tang institutions, the categories for recruiting scholars largely followed Sui precedents, yet in broad outline there were three.

units.zh: 由學館者曰生徒，由州縣者曰鄉貢，皆升於有司而進退之。
units.en: Candidates from state schools were called "student disciples"; those recommended by prefectures and counties were called "local tribute." Both were forwarded to the responsible offices, which decided who advanced and who did not.
units.literal: Those coming through academies were called student disciples; those coming through prefectures and counties were called local tribute; all were advanced to the competent offices, which promoted or rejected them.

units.zh: 其科之目，有秀才，有明經，有俊士，有進士，有明法，有明字，有明算，有一史，有三史，有開元禮，有道舉，有童子。
units.en: Examination categories included Xiucai (literary talent), Mingjing (classics), Junshi (outstanding scholars), Jinshi (presented scholars), Mingfa (law), Mingzi (writing), Mingsuan (mathematics), one-history and three-history examinations, Kaiyuan Rites, Daoist recommendation, and Tongzi (child prodigy).
units.literal: The categories of examinations included Xiucai, Mingjing, Junshi, Jinshi, Mingfa, Mingzi, Mingsuan, one-history, three-history, Kaiyuan Rites, Daoist recommendation, and Tongzi.

units.zh: 而明經之別，有五經，有三經，有二經，有學究一經，有三禮，有三傳，有史科。
units.en: Mingjing itself was subdivided into five-classics, three-classics, two-classics, single-classic specialized study, Three Rites, Three Commentaries, and history examinations.
units.literal: The subdivisions of Mingjing were Five Classics, Three Classics, Two Classics, one-classic specialized study, Three Rites, Three Commentaries, and history examinations.

units.zh: 此歲舉之常選也。
units.en: These were the routine annual examinations.
units.literal: These were the regular selections held each year.

units.zh: 其天子自詔者曰制舉，所以待非常之才焉。
units.en: Examinations specially proclaimed by the emperor were called "decree examinations," reserved for recruiting exceptional talent.
units.literal: Those personally summoned by edict of the Son of Heaven were called decree examinations, by which extraordinary talent was recruited.

units.zh: 凡學六，皆隸於國子監：國子學，生三百人，以文武三品以上子孫若從二品以上曾孫及勳官二品、縣公、京官四品帶三品勳封之子為之；
units.en: There were six schools, all under the Directorate of Education. The National University enrolled three hundred students: descendants of civil and military officials of the third rank and above; great-grandsons of collateral kin of the second rank and above; and sons of meritorious officials of the second rank, county dukes, and fourth-rank capital officials who held third-rank merit titles and enfeoffments.
units.literal: In all there were six schools, all subordinate to the Directorate of Education: the National University, with three hundred students, drawn from descendants of civil and military officials of the third rank and above, or great-grandsons of collateral second rank and above, and sons of meritorious officials of the second rank, county dukes, and capital officials of the fourth rank bearing third-rank merit titles and enfeoffments;

units.zh: 太學，生五百人，以五品以上子孫、職事官五品期親若三品曾孫及勳官三品以上有封之子為之；
units.en: The Great Academy took five hundred students: descendants of officials of the fifth rank and above; close relatives of fifth-rank active-duty officials or great-grandsons of third-rank officials; and sons of meritorious officials of the third rank and above who held enfeoffments.
units.literal: The Great Academy, five hundred students, drawn from descendants of officials of the fifth rank and above, close kin of fifth-rank active-duty officials or great-grandsons of third-rank officials, and sons of meritorious officials of the third rank and above who held enfeoffments;

units.zh: 四門學，生千三百人，其五百人以勳官三品以上無封、四品有封及文武七品以上子為之，八百人以庶人之俊異者為之；
units.en: The Four Gates Academy enrolled thirteen hundred students. Five hundred places went to sons of meritorious third-rank officials without enfeoffment, fourth-rank officials with enfeoffment, and civil or military officials of the seventh rank and above; eight hundred went to exceptionally talented commoners.
units.literal: The Four Gates Academy, thirteen hundred students: five hundred drawn from sons of meritorious officials of the third rank and above without enfeoffment, fourth-rank officials with enfeoffment, and civil and military officials of the seventh rank and above; eight hundred drawn from outstanding commoners;

units.zh: 律學，生五十人，書學，生三十人，算學，生三十人，以八品以下子及庶人之通其學者為之。
units.en: The Law School had fifty students; the Writing School and Mathematics School each had thirty, drawn from sons of officials below the eighth rank and commoners who had mastered those subjects.
units.literal: The Law School, fifty students; the Writing School, thirty; the Mathematics School, thirty—drawn from sons of officials below the eighth rank and commoners who had mastered those disciplines.

units.zh: 京都學生八十人，大都督、中都督府、上州各六十人，下都督府、中州各五十人，下州四十人，京縣五十人，上縣四十人，中縣、中下縣各三十五人，下縣二十人。
units.en: Quotas were: eighty students in the capital district; sixty each in great and middle military prefectures and upper prefectures; fifty each in lower military prefectures and middle prefectures; forty in lower prefectures; fifty in capital counties; forty in upper counties; thirty-five each in middle and lower-middle counties; and twenty in lower counties.
units.literal: Capital district schools, eighty students; great and middle area-command prefectures and upper prefectures, sixty each; lower area-command prefectures and middle prefectures, fifty each; lower prefectures, forty; capital counties, fifty; upper counties, forty; middle and lower-middle counties, thirty-five each; lower counties, twenty.

units.zh: 國子監生，尚書省補，祭酒統焉。
units.en: Students at the Directorate of Education were appointed by the Department of State Affairs and placed under the libationer's authority.
units.literal: Students of the Directorate of Education were appointed by the Department of State Affairs and overseen by the libationer.

units.zh: 州縣學生，州縣長官補，長史主焉。
units.en: Prefectural and county students were appointed by local magistrates and supervised by the chief secretary.
units.literal: Prefectural and county students were appointed by prefectural and county chiefs and administered by the chief secretary.

units.zh: 凡館二：門下省有弘文館，生三十人；
units.en: There were two academies: the Hongwen Academy under the Secretariat, with thirty students;
units.literal: In all there were two academies: under the Secretariat was the Hongwen Academy, thirty students;

units.zh: 東宮有崇文館，生二十人。
units.en: and the Chongwen Academy in the Eastern Palace, with twenty students.
units.literal: the Eastern Palace had the Chongwen Academy, twenty students.

units.zh: 以皇緦麻以上親，皇太后、皇后大功以上親，宰相及散官一品、功臣身食實封者、京官職事從三品、中書黃門侍郎之子為之。
units.en: Enrollment was limited to imperial relatives within the zimama degree and closer; relatives of the empress dowager and empress within the dagong degree and closer; and sons of chancellors, first-rank honorary officials, meritorious officials receiving substantive enfeoffment income, capital active-duty officials of the junior third rank, and Secretariat and Chancellery vice-directors.
units.literal: They were drawn from imperial kin within the zimama degree and closer, kin of the empress dowager and empress within the dagong degree and closer, sons of chancellors and first-rank honorary officials, meritorious officials receiving substantive enfeoffment income, and sons of capital active-duty officials of the junior third rank and of Secretariat and Chancellery vice-directors.

units.zh: 凡博士、助教，分經授諸生，未終經者無易業。
units.en: Erudites and teaching assistants taught the classics in separate sections; students who had not completed a classic could not switch subjects.
units.literal: Erudites and teaching assistants lectured on the classics separately to the students; those who had not finished a classic might not change their field of study.

units.zh: 凡生，限年十四以上，十九以下；
units.en: Students were generally required to be between fourteen and nineteen years of age;
units.literal: For students in general, the age limit was fourteen and above, nineteen and below;

units.zh: 律學十八以上，二十五以下。
units.en: for the Law School, between eighteen and twenty-five.
units.literal: for the Law School, eighteen and above, twenty-five and below.

units.zh: 凡《禮記》、《春秋左氏傳》為大經，《詩》、《周禮》、《儀禮》為中經，《易》、《尚書》、《春秋公羊傳》、《谷梁傳》為小經。
units.en: The Record of Rites and the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn were classified as major classics; the Odes, Rites of Zhou, and Ceremonial Rites as middle classics; and the Changes, Documents, Gongyang Commentary, and Guliang Commentary as minor classics.
units.literal: The Record of Rites and the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn were major classics; the Odes, Rites of Zhou, and Ceremonial Rites were middle classics; the Changes, Documents, Gongyang Commentary, and Guliang Commentary were minor classics.

units.zh: 通二經者，大經、小經各一，若中經二。
units.en: Mastery of two classics required one major and one minor classic, or two middle classics.
units.literal: To master two classics required one major and one minor, or two middle classics.

units.zh: 通三經者，大經、中經、小經各一。
units.en: Mastery of three classics required one major, one middle, and one minor classic.
units.literal: To master three classics required one each of major, middle, and minor.

units.zh: 通五經者，大經皆通，餘經各一，《孝經》、《論語》皆兼通之。
units.en: Mastery of five classics required all major classics, one each of the remaining classics, and proficiency in both the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects.
units.literal: To master five classics required all major classics plus one each of the remaining classics, with both the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects mastered as well.

units.zh: 凡治《孝經》、《論語》共限一歲，《尚書》、《公羊傳》、《谷梁傳》各一歲半，《易》、《詩》、《周禮》、《儀禮》各二歲，《禮記》、《左氏傳》各三歲。
units.en: Time limits for study were: one year for the Classic of Filial Piety and Analects together; one and a half years each for the Documents, Gongyang Commentary, and Guliang Commentary; two years each for the Changes, Odes, Rites of Zhou, and Ceremonial Rites; and three years each for the Record of Rites and Zuo Commentary.
units.literal: Study of the Classic of Filial Piety and Analects together was limited to one year; the Documents, Gongyang Commentary, and Guliang Commentary, one and a half years each; the Changes, Odes, Rites of Zhou, and Ceremonial Rites, two years each; the Record of Rites and Zuo Commentary, three years each.

units.zh: 學書，日紙一幅，間習時務策，讀《國語》、《說文》、《字林》、《三蒼》、《爾雅》。
units.en: Writing students copied one sheet of paper daily, practiced current-affairs policy questions in between, and read the Discourses of the States, Shuowen, Zilin, Sancang, and Erya.
units.literal: In the study of writing, one sheet of paper per day; between times they practiced current-affairs policy questions and read the Discourses of the States, Shuowen, Zilin, Sancang, and Erya.

units.zh: 凡書學，石經三體限三歲，《說文》二歲，《字林》一歲。
units.en: In the Writing School, the three stone-classic scripts required three years of study, the Shuowen two years, and the Zilin one year.
units.literal: For the Writing School, the three stone-classic scripts were limited to three years, the Shuowen to two, the Zilin to one.

units.zh: 凡算學，《孫子》、《五曹》共限一歲，《九章》、《海島》共三歲，《張丘建》、《夏侯陽》各一歲，《周髀》、《五經算》共一歲，《綴術》四歲，《緝古》三歲，《記遺》、《三等數》皆兼習之。
units.en: Mathematics students studied the Sunzi and Wucao together for one year; the Jiuzhang and Haidao for three years together; the Zhang Qiujian and Xiahou Yang for one year each; the Zhoubi and Wujing suan for one year together; the Zhui shu for four years; the Jigu for three years; and the Jiyi and Sandeng shu alongside all of these.
units.literal: For the Mathematics School, the Sunzi and Wucao together one year; the Jiuzhang and Haidao together three years; the Zhang Qiujian and Xiahou Yang one year each; the Zhoubi and Wujing suan together one year; the Zhui shu four years; the Jigu three years; the Jiyi and Sandeng shu were studied together with all of these.

units.zh: 旬給假一日。
units.en: Students received one day of leave every ten days.
units.literal: Every ten days one day of leave was granted.

units.zh: 前假，博士考試，讀者千言試一帖，帖三言，講者二千言問大義一條，總三條通二為第，不及者有罰。
units.en: Before each leave period, erudites tested students: readers faced one slip test per thousand characters (three characters per slip); lecturers answered one question on major principles per two thousand characters. Passing two of three questions counted as a pass; failure brought punishment.
units.literal: Before leave, erudites examined them: readers were tested on one slip per thousand characters, three characters per slip; lecturers were questioned on one major principle per two thousand characters; of three questions in all, passing two constituted a grade; those who did not meet the standard were punished.

units.zh: 歲終，通一年之業，口問大義十條，通八為上，六為中，五為下。
units.en: At year's end, after completing the annual curriculum, students answered ten oral questions on major principles: eight correct answers ranked as upper, six as middle, and five as lower.
units.literal: At year's end, having completed the year's curriculum, they were orally questioned on ten major principles; passing eight was upper, six middle, five lower.

units.zh: 並三下與在學九歲、律生六歲不堪貢者罷歸。
units.en: Students who ranked in the lower grade, as well as those who after nine years in school—or six years in the Law School—were still unfit for presentation, were dismissed and sent home.
units.literal: Those with lower grade together with those who after nine years in school or six years as law students were unfit for tribute presentation were dismissed and sent home.

units.zh: 諸學生通二經、俊士通三經已及第而願留者，四門學生補太學，太學生補國子學。
units.en: Students who had mastered two classics, or Junshi who had mastered three classics and already passed but wished to continue studying, advanced from the Four Gates Academy to the Great Academy, and from the Great Academy to the National University.
units.literal: Students who had mastered two classics and Junshi who had mastered three classics and already passed the examinations but wished to remain were transferred from the Four Gates Academy to the Great Academy, and from the Great Academy to the National University.

units.zh: 每歲五月有田假，九月有授衣假，二百里外給程。
units.en: Each year students received field-work leave in the fifth month and clothing leave in the ninth month; those living more than two hundred li away were granted travel time.
units.literal: Each year in the fifth month there was field-work leave; in the ninth month, clothing-distribution leave; for those beyond two hundred li, travel time was allowed.

units.zh: 其不帥教及歲中違程滿三十日，事故百日，緣親病二百日，皆罷歸。
units.en: Students who defied instruction, exceeded thirty days of unauthorized absence in a year, took one hundred days for personal affairs, or two hundred days to care for ill relatives were all dismissed and sent home.
units.literal: Those who did not follow instruction, or within the year exceeded permitted absence by thirty days, or one hundred days for personal affairs, or two hundred days for illness of kin, were all dismissed and sent home.

units.zh: 既罷，條其狀下之屬所，五品以上子孫送兵部，准廕配色。
units.en: Upon dismissal, their records were forwarded to the appropriate office; descendants of fifth-rank officials and above were referred to the Ministry of War for hereditary appointment and uniform assignment.
units.literal: Once dismissed, their circumstances were itemized and sent down to the subordinate office; descendants of fifth rank and above were sent to the Ministry of War for hereditary appointment and assignment of colors.

units.zh: 每歲仲冬，州、縣、館、監舉其成者送之尚書省；
units.en: Each year in mid-winter, prefectures, counties, academies, and the directorate sent their qualified students to the Department of State Affairs;
units.literal: Every year in mid-winter, prefectures, counties, academies, and directorates presented their successful students and sent them to the Department of State Affairs;

units.zh: 而舉選不繇館、學者，謂之鄉貢，皆懷牒自列於州、縣。
units.en: candidates who did not come through academies or schools were called "local tribute" and registered themselves at their prefecture or county with their credentials in hand.
units.literal: those presenting themselves for selection who did not come through academies or schools were called local tribute; all carried their dossiers and registered themselves at prefectures and counties.

units.zh: 試已，長吏以鄉飲酒禮，會屬僚，設賓主，陳俎豆，備管弦，牲用少牢，歌《鹿鳴》之詩，因與耆艾敘長少焉。
units.en: After the local examination, the magistrate held a district drinking ceremony with his staff, arranging host and guest, setting out offerings, providing music, sacrificing with the lesser pen ritual, singing the "Deer Cry" ode, and with village elders discussing the order of seniority.
units.literal: After the examination, the chief official held the district drinking ceremony, gathering subordinate officials, setting host and guest, displaying meat and grain offerings, providing string and wind instruments, using the lesser pen sacrifice, singing the "Luming" ode, and thereupon with elders discussing senior and junior order.

units.zh: 既至省，皆疏名列到，結款通保及所居，始由戶部集閱，而關於考功員外郎試之。
units.en: Upon reaching the capital, candidates listed their names and registered arrival, submitted mutual guarantees and addresses, underwent review by the Ministry of Revenue, and were then examined by the vice-director of the Ministry of Personnel.
units.literal: Once they reached the capital, all listed their names in memorial and registered arrival, made sworn bonds of mutual guarantee and stated their residence; only then did the Ministry of Revenue assemble and review them, and the matter was referred to the vice-director of the Ministry of Personnel for examination.

units.zh: 凡秀才，試方略策五道，以文理通粗為上上、上中、上下、中上，凡四等為及第。
units.en: Xiucai candidates answered five policy-and-strategy questions. Those whose writing showed general coherence received one of four passing grades: upper-upper, upper-middle, upper-lower, or middle-upper.
units.literal: For Xiucai, five policy-and-strategy questions were tested; those whose literary reasoning was generally coherent were graded upper-upper, upper-middle, upper-lower, and middle-upper—four grades in all counted as passing.

units.zh: 凡明經，先帖文，然後口試，經問大義十條，答時務策三道，亦為四等。
units.en: Mingjing candidates first faced text-quotation tests, then oral examination: ten questions on major principles of the classics and three current-affairs policy questions, graded in four ranks.
units.literal: For Mingjing, text quotation came first, then oral examination: ten questions on major principles of the classics, three answers to current-affairs policy questions—also four grades.

units.zh: 凡《開元禮》，通大義百條、策三道者，超資與官；
units.en: For the Kaiyuan Rites examination, candidates who passed one hundred questions on major principles and three policy questions received extraordinary promotion and appointment;
units.literal: For the Kaiyuan Rites, those who passed one hundred major principles and three policy questions received extraordinary promotion and appointment;

units.zh: 義通七十、策通二者，及第。
units.en: those who passed seventy principle questions and two policy questions were considered to have passed.
units.literal: those who passed seventy on principles and two on policy questions passed.

units.zh: 散、試官能通者，依正員。
units.en: Honorary and probationary officials who passed were treated the same as regular appointees.
units.literal: Honorary and probationary officials who could pass were treated like regular appointees.

units.zh: 凡三傳科，《左氏傳》問大義五十條，《公羊》、《谷梁傳》三十條，策皆三道，義通七以上、策通二以上為第，白身視五經，有出身及前資官視學究一經。
units.en: The Three Commentaries examination required fifty questions on the Zuo Commentary and thirty each on the Gongyang and Guliang, plus three policy questions. Passing seven principle questions and two policy questions counted as a pass. Commoners were ranked like five-classics graduates; those already holding office or former rank were ranked like single-classic specialists.
units.literal: For the Three Commentaries examination, fifty major principles on the Zuo Commentary, thirty each on the Gongyang and Guliang; three policy questions for all; passing seven or more on principles and two or more on policy counted as a grade; commoners were treated like five-classics candidates, those with prior appointment or former rank like one-classic specialized study.

units.zh: 凡史科，每史問大義百條、策三道，義通七、策通二以上為第。
units.en: History examinations posed one hundred questions on major principles and three policy questions per history; passing seven principle questions and two policy questions counted as a pass.
units.literal: For history examinations, each history had one hundred major principles and three policy questions; passing seven on principles and two on policy counted as a grade.

units.zh: 能通一史者，白身視五經、三傳，有出身及前資官視學究一經；
units.en: Those who mastered one history were ranked like five-classics or three-commentaries graduates if commoners, or like single-classic specialists if they already held office or former rank;
units.literal: Those who mastered one history: commoners were treated like five-classics or three-commentaries graduates; those with prior appointment or former rank like one-classic specialized study;

units.zh: 三史皆通者，獎擢之。
units.en: those who mastered all three histories received special promotion.
units.literal: those who mastered all three histories were specially promoted and selected.

units.zh: 凡童子科，十歲以下能通一經及《孝經》、《論語》，卷誦文十，通者予官；
units.en: For the child-prodigy examination, candidates under ten who had mastered one classic plus the Classic of Filial Piety and Analects recited ten passages from a scroll; those who passed all ten received immediate appointment;
units.literal: For the Tongzi examination, those under ten who could master one classic and the Classic of Filial Piety and Analects: of ten passages recited from a scroll, those who passed received appointment;

units.zh: 通七，予出身。
units.en: passing seven received qualification for future office.
units.literal: passing seven received qualification for office.

units.zh: 凡進士，試時務策五道、帖一大經，經、策全通為甲第；
units.en: Jinshi candidates answered five current-affairs policy questions and faced text-quotation from one major classic. Passing both completely earned first grade;
units.literal: For Jinshi, five current-affairs policy questions and quotation from one major classic were tested; full passage on both classics and policy was first grade;

units.zh: 策通四、帖過四以上為乙第。
units.en: passing four policy questions and four or more quotation slips earned second grade.
units.literal: passing four policy questions and more than four on quotation was second grade.

units.zh: 凡明法，試律七條、令三條，全通為甲第，通八為乙第。
units.en: Law candidates were tested on seven statutes and three administrative regulations. Passing all earned first grade; passing eight earned second grade.
units.literal: For Mingfa, seven statutes and three administrative regulations were tested; full passage was first grade, passing eight was second grade.

units.zh: 凡書學，先口試，通，乃墨試《說文》、《字林》二十條，通十八為第。
units.en: Writing candidates first took an oral examination; if they passed, they faced a written test on twenty items from the Shuowen and Zilin. Passing eighteen counted as a pass.
units.literal: For the Writing School, oral examination came first; upon passing, written examination on twenty items from the Shuowen and Zilin—passing eighteen counted as a grade.

units.zh: 凡算學，錄大義本條為問答，明數造術，詳明術理，然後為通。
units.en: Mathematics candidates answered questions drawn from major principles in the texts; they had to demonstrate numerical clarity, construct methods correctly, and explain the reasoning in detail before they could pass.
units.literal: For the Mathematics School, major principles were recorded item by item as questions and answers; clarity in numbers and construction of methods, and detailed explanation of method and principle, were required before passing.

units.zh: 試《九章》三條、《海島》《孫子》《五曹》《張丘建》《夏侯陽》《周髀》《五經算》各一條，十通六，《記遺》、《三等數》帖讀十得九，為第。
units.en: The examination included three questions on the Jiuzhang and one each on seven other mathematical texts; passing six of ten counted as a pass. For the Jiyi and Sandeng shu, candidates read ten quotation slips and needed nine correct.
units.literal: Three questions on the Jiuzhang, one each on the Haidao, Sunzi, Wucao, Zhang Qiujian, Xiahou Yang, Zhoubi, and Wujing suan—passing six of ten; for the Jiyi and Sandeng shu, quotation reading ten with nine correct counted as a grade.

units.zh: 試《綴術》、《輯古》，錄大義為問答者，明數造術，詳明術理，無注者合數造術，不失義理，然後為通。
units.en: For the Zhui shu and Jigu examinations, candidates answered questions on major principles, demonstrating numerical clarity and sound method. Where texts lacked annotations, they had to derive methods from the numbers without violating the underlying principles.
units.literal: For examination on the Zhui shu and Jigu, recording major principles as questions and answers: clarity in numbers and construction of methods, detailed explanation of method and principle; where there were no annotations, constructing methods from the numbers without losing the principle—only then was passing granted.

units.zh: 《綴術》七條、《輯古》三條，十通六，《記遺》、《三等數》帖讀十得九，為第。
units.en: The Zhui shu examination had seven questions and the Jigu three; passing six of ten counted as a pass. For the Jiyi and Sandeng shu, reading ten quotation slips with nine correct also counted as passing.
units.literal: Seven questions on the Zhui shu and three on the Jigu—passing six of ten; for the Jiyi and Sandeng shu, quotation reading ten with nine correct counted as a grade.

units.zh: 落經者，雖通六，不第。
units.en: Candidates who failed the classic portion did not pass, even if they answered six questions correctly overall.
units.literal: Those who failed the classic portion, even if passing six overall, did not receive a grade.

units.zh: 凡弘文、崇文生，試一大經、一小經，或二中經，或《史記》、《前後漢書》、《三國志》各一，或時務策五道。
units.en: Hongwen and Chongwen students were examined on one major and one minor classic, or two middle classics, or one each from the Records of the Grand Historian, Book of Han, Book of Later Han, and Records of the Three Kingdoms, or five current-affairs policy questions.
units.literal: For Hongwen and Chongwen students, one major and one minor classic, or two middle classics, or one each of the Records of the Grand Historian, Book of Han, Book of Later Han, and Records of the Three Kingdoms, or five current-affairs policy questions were tested.

units.zh: 經史皆試策十道。
units.en: Whether candidates took classics or histories, they also answered ten policy questions.
units.literal: For classics and histories alike, ten policy questions were tested.

units.zh: 經通六，史及時務策通三，皆帖《孝經》、《論語》共十條通六，為第。
units.en: Candidates passed by answering six classic questions correctly, three history or policy questions correctly, and six of ten quotation slips from the Classic of Filial Piety and Analects.
units.literal: Passing six on classics, three on history or current-affairs policy, and six of ten quotations from the Classic of Filial Piety and Analects counted as a grade.

units.zh: 凡貢舉非其人者、廢舉者、校試不以實者，皆有罰。
units.en: Officials who recommended unqualified candidates, failed to recommend qualified ones, or conducted examinations dishonestly were all subject to punishment.
units.literal: For presenting unworthy persons, abandoning presentation, or examining without truthfulness, penalties were imposed in all cases.

units.zh: 其教人取士著於令者，大略如此。
units.en: The statutory provisions on education and recruitment were, in broad outline, as described above.
units.literal: The regulations on educating people and recruiting scholars were in broad outline as described above.

units.zh: 而士之進取之方，與上之好惡、所以育材養士、招來獎進之意，有司選士之法，因時增損不同。
units.en: Yet the paths by which scholars advanced, the ruler's changing preferences, the aims of nurturing talent and rewarding achievement, and the methods offices used to select candidates all shifted over time with additions and cuts.
units.literal: Yet the methods by which scholars advanced, the preferences of the ruler above, the intent to nurture talent and cultivate scholars and to recruit and reward advancement, and the methods by which offices selected scholars—all differed as times changed with additions and reductions.

units.zh: 自高祖初入長安，開大丞相府，下令置生員，自京師至於州縣皆有數。
units.en: When Gaozu first entered Chang'an and opened the Grand Chancellor's Office, he ordered student quotas established at every level from the capital down to prefectures and counties.
units.literal: From the time Gaozu first entered Chang'an and opened the Grand Chancellor's Office, he issued orders to establish student quotas, with fixed numbers from the capital down to prefectures and counties.

units.zh: 既即位，又詔秘書外省別立小學，以教宗室子孫及功臣子弟。
units.en: After his enthronement, he also ordered a separate elementary school outside the Secretariat to educate imperial clan descendants and sons of meritorious officials.
units.literal: After he took the throne, he also ordered a separate elementary school established outside the Secretariat to teach imperial clan descendants and sons of meritorious officials.

units.zh: 其後又詔諸州明經、秀才、俊士、進士明于理體為鄉里稱者，縣考試，州長重覆，歲隨方物入貢；
units.en: He later ordered that throughout the empire, candidates in Mingjing, Xiucai, Junshi, and Jinshi who showed mastery of principle and were acclaimed locally should be examined by their county, re-examined by the prefect, and sent annually to court with local tribute;
units.literal: Later he also ordered that in all prefectures those in Mingjing, Xiucai, Junshi, and Jinshi who were clear in principle and structure and acclaimed in their districts should be examined by the county, re-examined by the prefect, and each year sent in tribute with local products;

units.zh: 吏民子弟學藝者，皆送於京學，為設考課之法。
units.en: sons of officials and commoners studying the arts were all sent to capital schools, and examination regulations were established for them.
units.literal: sons of officials and commoners who studied arts were all sent to the capital schools, for which examination regulations were established.

units.zh: 州、縣、鄉皆置學焉。
units.en: Schools were established at the prefectural, county, and district levels.
units.literal: Schools were established in prefectures, counties, and districts alike.

units.zh: 及太宗即位，益崇儒術。
units.en: When Taizong came to the throne, he gave even greater prominence to Confucian learning.
units.literal: When Taizong took the throne, he further honored Confucian learning.

units.zh: 乃于門下別置弘文館，又增置書、律學，進士加讀經、史一部。
units.en: He established the Hongwen Academy under the Secretariat, added Writing and Law schools, and required Jinshi candidates to study an additional classic or historical work.
units.literal: He then separately established the Hongwen Academy under the Secretariat, also added Writing and Law schools, and required Jinshi candidates to read an additional classic or history.

units.zh: 十三年，東宮置崇文館。
units.en: In his thirteenth year, the Eastern Palace established the Chongwen Academy.
units.literal: In the thirteenth year, the Eastern Palace established the Chongwen Academy.

units.zh: 自天下初定，增築學舍至千二百區，雖七營飛騎，亦置生，遣博士為授經。
units.en: After the empire was pacified, school buildings increased to twelve hundred wards. Even the seven camps of flying cavalry enrolled students and were assigned erudites to teach the classics.
units.literal: From the time the realm was first pacified, school buildings were increased to twelve hundred wards; even the seven camps of flying cavalry had students placed, with erudites dispatched to lecture on the classics.

units.zh: 四夷若高麗、百濟、新羅、高昌、吐蕃，相繼遣子弟入學，遂至八千餘人。
units.en: Foreign states including Koguryo, Paekche, Silla, Gaochang, and Tibet successively sent princes and sons to study, until enrollment exceeded eight thousand.
units.literal: Barbarians of the four directions such as Koguryo, Paekche, Silla, Gaochang, and Tibet sent sons in succession to study, until there were more than eight thousand persons.

units.zh: 高宗永徽二年，始停秀才科。
units.en: In Gaozong's second Yonghui year (651), the Xiucai examination was abolished.
units.literal: In the second year of Yonghui under Gaozong, the Xiucai examination was first suspended.

units.zh: 龍朔二年，東都置國子監，明年以書學隸蘭台，算學隸秘閣，律學隸詳刑。
units.en: In 662, the Directorate of Education was established in the eastern capital. The following year the Writing School was placed under the Orchid Terrace, the Mathematics School under the Secret Archive, and the Law School under Detailed Punishments.
units.literal: In the second year of Longshuo, the Directorate of Education was established in the eastern capital; the next year the Writing School was placed under the Orchid Terrace, the Mathematics School under the Secret Archive, and the Law School under the Detailed Punishments office.

units.zh: 上元二年，加試貢士《老子》策，明經二條，進士三條。
units.en: In 675, candidates were also tested on the Laozi: two policy questions for Mingjing candidates and three for Jinshi.
units.literal: In the second year of Shangyuan, Laozi's Classic was added to the examination policy questions for tribute scholars—two questions for Mingjing, three for Jinshi.

units.zh: 國子監置大成二十人，取已及第而聰明者為之。
units.en: The Directorate of Education appointed twenty Great Achievers, selected from examination graduates who showed exceptional ability.
units.literal: The Directorate of Education established twenty Great Achievers, drawn from those who had already passed the examinations and were intelligent.

units.zh: 試書日誦千言，並日試策，所業十通七，然後補其祿俸，同直官。
units.en: They recited a thousand characters daily in writing tests and took daily policy examinations. After passing seven of ten subjects, they received salaries equal to regular-duty officials.
units.literal: They were tested in writing with a thousand characters recited per day, and policy questions tested daily; of ten subjects mastered, passing seven—only then were they granted salary, equal to regular-duty officials.

units.zh: 通四經業成，上于尚書，吏部試之，登第者加一階放選。
units.en: After mastering four classics, they were reported to the Department of State Affairs and examined by the Ministry of Personnel. Those who passed received one additional rank in the appointment roster.
units.literal: When four classics were mastered and their studies completed, they were reported to the Department of State Affairs; the Ministry of Personnel examined them, and those who passed received one additional rank in appointment selection.

units.zh: 其不第則習業如初，三歲而又試，三試而不中第，從常調。
units.en: Those who failed resumed their studies. After three years they were examined again; if they failed three times, they entered the regular appointment rotation.
units.literal: Those who did not pass resumed study as at first; after three years they were examined again; if they failed to pass after three examinations, they followed regular appointment rotation.

units.zh: 永隆二年，考功員外郎劉思立建言，明經多抄義條，進士唯誦舊策，皆亡實才，而有司以人數充第。
units.en: In 681, Vice-Director Liu Sili memorialized that Mingjing candidates mostly copied textbook entries, while Jinshi merely recited old examination answers—neither showed real ability, yet officials passed candidates merely to fill quotas.
units.literal: In the second year of Yonglong, Vice-Director of Personnel Liu Sili submitted a memorial: Mingjing candidates mostly copied principle entries; Jinshi merely recited old policy answers—all lacked real talent, yet the offices filled quotas by head count.

units.zh: 乃詔自今明經試帖粗十得六以上，進士試雜文二篇，通文律者然後試策。
units.en: An edict followed: henceforth Mingjing candidates had to pass text-quotation tests with six of ten slips correct; Jinshi candidates had to pass two literary essays before taking policy examinations.
units.literal: An edict was therefore issued: from now on Mingjing would test text quotation with six of ten coarse slips correct; Jinshi would test two miscellaneous essays, and only those who passed literary rules would then be tested on policy questions.

units.zh: 武后之亂，改易舊制頗多。
units.en: During Empress Wu's reign, many longstanding institutions were altered.
units.literal: During the turmoil of Empress Wu, many old institutions were changed.

units.zh: 中宗反正，詔宗室三等以下、五等以上未出身，願宿衛及任國子生，聽之。
units.en: After Zhongzong's restoration, he decreed that imperial clansmen of the third rank and below and fifth rank and above who had not yet received office might serve in the palace guard or enroll as National University students if they wished.
units.literal: When Zhongzong restored the proper order, he decreed that imperial clansmen of the third rank and below and fifth rank and above who had not yet received appointment, if they wished to serve in the palace guard or take office as National University students, were permitted to do so.

units.zh: 其家居業成而堪貢者，宗正寺試，送監舉如常法。
units.en: Clansmen who completed their studies at home and were fit for presentation were examined by the Imperial Clan Court and forwarded to the directorate by the usual procedure.
units.literal: Those who at home completed their studies and were fit for tribute presentation were examined by the Imperial Clan Court and sent to the directorate for presentation by the usual method.

units.zh: 三衛番下日，願入學者，聽附國子學、太學及律館習業。
units.en: When guards of the Three Guards rotated off duty, those who wished to study were permitted to enroll in the National University, Great Academy, or Law School.
units.literal: On days when the Three Guards rotated off duty, those who wished to enter study were permitted to attach to the National University, Great Academy, and Law School for their studies.

units.zh: 蕃王及可汗子孫願入學者，附國子學讀書。
units.en: Sons and grandsons of foreign kings and khans who wished to study were enrolled in the National University.
units.literal: Sons and grandsons of barbarian kings and khans who wished to enter study attached to the National University for reading.

units.zh: 玄宗開元五年，始令鄉貢明經、進士見訖，國子監謁先師，學官開講問義，有司為具食，清資五品以上官及朝集使皆往閱禮焉。
units.en: In 717, Xuanzong ordered that after their audience, local-tribute Mingjing and Jinshi candidates visit the Confucian temple at the Directorate of Education, where instructors lectured and discussed the classics. The government provided a feast, and fifth-rank officials and assembly envoys attended to observe the rites.
units.literal: In the fifth year of Kaiyuan under Xuanzong, it was first ordered that after local-tribute Mingjing and Jinshi candidates had completed their audience, they should visit the sage at the Directorate of Education; academic officials opened lectures and questioned on principles; the offices provided food; officials of pure appointment of the fifth rank and above and assembly envoys all went to observe the ceremony.

units.zh: 七年，又令弘文、崇文、國子生季一朝參。
units.en: In 719, he also required Hongwen, Chongwen, and National University students to attend court once each season.
units.literal: In the seventh year, it was further ordered that Hongwen, Chongwen, and National University students attend court once each season.

units.zh: 及注《老子道德經》成，詔天下家藏其書，貢舉人滅《尚書》、《論語》策，而加試《老子》。
units.en: When Xuanzong finished his commentary on the Laozi, he ordered every household to keep a copy. Examination candidates faced fewer policy questions on the Documents and Analects, and the Laozi was added to the test.
units.literal: When the commentary on the Laozi's Classic of the Way and Virtue was completed, an edict ordered every household in the realm to keep a copy; tribute candidates had their policy questions on the Documents and Analects reduced, and the Laozi was added to the examination.

units.zh: 又敕州縣學生年二十五以下、八品子若庶人二十一以下通一經及未通經而聰悟有文辭、史學者，入四門學為俊士。
units.en: He further decreed that prefectural and county students under twenty-five, sons of eighth-rank officials or commoners under twenty-one who had mastered one classic—or who showed literary or historical talent even without completing a classic—could enter the Four Gates Academy as Junshi.
units.literal: It was further ordered that prefectural and county students twenty-five and below, sons of eighth-rank officials or commoners twenty-one and below who had mastered one classic, or who had not mastered a classic but were intelligent with literary skill or historical learning, should enter the Four Gates Academy as Junshi.

units.zh: 即諸州貢舉省試不第，願入學者亦聽。
units.en: Candidates from the provinces who failed the capital examination but wished to continue studying were also permitted to enroll.
units.literal: That is, those from all prefectures who failed the provincial examination for tribute presentation but wished to enter study were also permitted.

units.zh: 二十四年，考功員外郎李昂為舉人詆訶，帝以員外郎望輕，遂移貢舉於禮部，以侍郎主之。
units.en: In 736, Vice-Director Li Ang was publicly insulted by candidates. The emperor considered the vice-director's rank too low and transferred the examinations to the Ministry of Rites, to be chaired by a vice-minister.
units.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, Vice-Director of Personnel Li Ang was reviled by candidates; the emperor considered the vice-director's standing too light, and therefore moved tribute presentation examinations to the Ministry of Rites, with a vice-minister presiding.

units.zh: 禮部選士自此始。
units.en: From this point the Ministry of Rites took charge of selecting scholars.
units.literal: The Ministry of Rites' selection of scholars began from this point.

units.zh: 二十九年，始置崇玄學，習《老子》、《莊子》、《文子》、《列子》，亦曰道舉。
units.en: In 741, the Chongxuan School was established to study the Laozi, Zhuangzi, Wenzi, and Liezi. It was also known as the Daoist recommendation examination.
units.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, the Chongxuan School was first established to study the Laozi, Zhuangzi, Wenzi, and Liezi—it was also called Daoist recommendation.

units.zh: 其生，京、都各百人，諸州無常員。
units.en: Enrollment was one hundred each in Chang'an and Luoyang; prefectures had no fixed quotas.
units.literal: Its students: one hundred each in the capital and eastern capital; prefectures had no fixed quotas.

units.zh: 官秩、廕第同國子，舉送、課試如明經。
units.en: Official ranks, hereditary privileges, presentation procedures, and examinations followed the same rules as the National University and Mingjing candidates.
units.literal: Official rank, hereditary privilege, and presentation and examination followed the same rules as the National University and Mingjing.

units.zh: 天寶九載，置廣文館于國學，以領生徒為進士者。
units.en: In 750, the Guangwen Academy was established within the National University to supervise students preparing for the Jinshi examination.
units.literal: In the ninth year of Tianbao, the Guangwen Academy was established within the National University to oversee students who were Jinshi candidates.

units.zh: 舉人舊重兩監，後世祿者以京兆、同、華為榮，而不入學。
units.en: Candidates had once prized enrollment in the two directorates of education; by later times, those seeking office took pride in qualifying through Jingzhao, Tongzhou, or Huazhou and no longer entered the schools at all.
units.literal: Candidates of old prized the two directorates; in later times those seeking salary took pride in Jingzhao, Tong, and Hua, and did not enter the schools.

units.zh: 十二載，乃敕天下罷鄉貢，舉人不由國子及郡、縣學者，勿舉送。
units.en: In 753, an edict abolished local tribute examinations empire-wide; candidates who had not passed through the National University or prefectural and county schools were not to be forwarded for examination.
units.literal: In the twelfth year, an edict abolished local tribute throughout the realm; candidates who had not come through the National University or prefectural and county schools were not to be presented.

units.zh: 是歲，道舉停《老子》，加《周易》。
units.en: That same year the Daoist recommendation examination dropped the Laozi and added the Book of Changes.
units.literal: That year, the Daoist examination dropped the Laozi and added the Book of Changes.

units.zh: 十四載，復鄉貢。
units.en: In 755, local tribute examinations were restored.
units.literal: In the fourteenth year, local tribute was restored.

units.zh: 代宗廣德二年，詔曰：「古者設太學，教胄子，雖年穀不登，兵革或動，而俎豆之事不廢。
units.en: In 764, Emperor Daizong issued an edict: "In antiquity the Imperial Academy was founded to instruct the sons of officials. Though harvests failed or armies took the field, sacrificial rites were never abandoned.
units.literal: In the second year of Guangde under Emperor Daizong, an edict said: "In antiquity the Imperial Academy was established to instruct the sons of officials; though harvests failed or armies marched, sacrificial rites were not abandoned.

units.zh: 頃年戎車屢駕，諸生輟講，宜追學生在館習業，度支給廚米。」
units.en: In recent years war has repeatedly broken out and students have ceased their studies. Students in residence should be recalled to continue their coursework, and the Department of Public Works should supply grain for their kitchens."
units.literal: In recent years war-chariots have repeatedly been deployed and students have ceased instruction; students in residence should be recalled to pursue their studies in the academies, and the Department of Public Works should supply kitchen grain."

units.zh: 是歲，賈至為侍郎，建言歲方艱歉，舉人赴省者，兩都試之。
units.en: That year Jia Zhi served as vice-minister of rites and proposed that, given the year's hardship and scarcity, candidates traveling to the capital should be examined in both capitals instead.
units.literal: That year, Jia Zhi was vice-minister and proposed that since the year was one of hardship and dearth, candidates coming to the capital should be examined in both capitals.

units.zh: 兩都試人自此始。
units.en: Dual-capital examinations began from this time.
units.literal: Examination of candidates in both capitals began from this point.

units.zh: 貞元二年，詔習《開元禮》者舉同一經例，明經習律以代《爾雅》。
units.en: In 786, an edict required candidates in the Kaiyuan Rites examination to follow the same rules as single-classic Mingjing candidates, and Mingjing candidates to study law codes in place of the Erya.
units.literal: In the second year of Zhenyuan, an edict ordered that those studying the Kaiyuan Rites be examined under the same rules as single-classic candidates, and that Mingjing candidates study law codes in place of the Erya.

units.zh: 是時弘文、崇文生未補者，務取員闕以補，速於登第，而用廕乖實，至有假市門資、變易昭穆及假人試藝者。
units.en: At that time Hongwen and Chongwen students awaiting appointment scrambled to fill vacant posts and pass examinations as quickly as possible. Hereditary privilege was widely abused: some forged market-gate credentials, altered their ancestral lineages, or hired substitutes to take the skill examinations for them.
units.literal: At that time Hongwen and Chongwen students not yet appointed sought vacancies to fill, rushing to pass the examinations; use of hereditary privilege did not match reality—there were even cases of falsifying market-gate credentials, altering lineages, and hiring substitutes to take skill examinations.

units.zh: 六年，詔宜據式考試，假代者論如法。
units.en: In 790, an edict required examinations to follow the prescribed regulations, and proxy candidates were to be punished according to law.
units.literal: In the sixth year, an edict ordered that examinations follow the regulations; proxy test-takers were to be prosecuted according to law.

units.zh: 初，禮部侍郎親故移試考功，謂之別頭。
units.en: Originally, relatives and associates of the vice-minister of rites were transferred to the Directorate of Personnel for examination—a separate track known as bietou, "separate head."
units.literal: Initially, relatives and associates of the Vice-Minister of Rites were transferred for examination to the Directorate of Personnel—this was called bietou, "separate head."

units.zh: 十六年，中書舍人高郢奏罷，議者是之。
units.en: In 800, Secretariat drafter Gao Ying memorialized to abolish the practice, and policy critics agreed.
units.literal: In the sixteenth year, Secretariat Drafter Gao Ying memorialized to abolish it; critics of policy approved.

units.zh: 元和二年，置東都監生一百員。
units.en: In 807, one hundred student places were established at the Eastern Capital directorate.
units.literal: In the second year of Yuanhe, one hundred Eastern Capital directorate students were established.

units.zh: 然自天寶後，學校益廢，生徒流散。
units.en: Yet after the Tianbao era schools fell increasingly into disuse and students scattered.
units.literal: Yet from after Tianbao, schools were increasingly abandoned and students dispersed.

units.zh: 永泰中，雖置西監生，而館無定員。
units.en: During the Yongtai era, although Western Capital directorate students were established, the academies had no fixed enrollment.
units.literal: In the Yongtai era, although Western directorate students were established, the academies had no fixed quotas.

units.zh: 於是始定生員：西京國子館生八十人，太學七十人，四門三百人，廣文六十人，律館二十人，書、算館各十人；
units.en: Student quotas were then fixed for the first time. At Chang'an: eighty National University hostel students, seventy Imperial University students, three hundred Four Gates students, sixty Guangwen students, twenty law-school students, and ten each in the writing and mathematics schools;
units.literal: Thereupon student quotas were first fixed: at the Western Capital, eighty National University hostel students, seventy Imperial University students, three hundred Four Gates students, sixty Guangwen students, twenty law-school students, and ten each in the writing and mathematics schools;

units.zh: 東都國子館十人，太學十五人，四門五十人，廣文十人，律館十人，書館三人，算館二人而已。
units.en: at Luoyang: ten National University hostel students, fifteen Imperial University students, fifty Four Gates students, ten Guangwen students, ten law-school students, three writing-school students, and two mathematics-school students—and no more.
units.literal: at the Eastern Capital, ten National University hostel students, fifteen Imperial University students, fifty Four Gates students, ten Guangwen students, ten law-school students, three writing-school students, and two mathematics-school students only.

units.zh: 明經停口義，復試墨義十條。
units.en: The Mingjing examination discontinued oral exposition and restored ten written ink-meaning questions.
units.literal: Mingjing discontinued oral exposition and restored ten written ink-meaning questions.

units.zh: 五經取通五，明經通六。
units.en: Five Classics candidates had to pass five questions; Mingjing candidates had to pass six.
units.literal: Five Classics required passing five; Mingjing required passing six.

units.zh: 其嘗坐法及為州縣小吏，雖藝文可采，勿舉。
units.en: Those who had been convicted under law or had served as petty prefectural and county clerks were not to be recommended, however talented their literary work.
units.literal: Those who had been punished by law or served as petty prefectural and county clerks, though their literary arts were acceptable, were not to be recommended.

units.zh: 十三年，權知禮部侍郎庾承宣奏復考功別頭試。
units.en: In 818, acting vice-minister of rites Yu Chengxuan memorialized to restore the separate-head examination at the Directorate of Personnel.
units.literal: In the thirteenth year, Acting Vice-Minister of Rites Yu Chengxuan memorialized to restore the Directorate of Personnel separate-head examination.

units.zh: 初，開元中，禮部考試畢，送中書門下詳覆，其後中廢。
units.en: Under Kaiyuan, after the Ministry of Rites completed its examinations, results were sent to the Secretariat for detailed review; later this practice was suspended.
units.literal: Initially, in the Kaiyuan era, after the Ministry of Rites finished its examinations, results were sent to the Secretariat for detailed review; later this was suspended midway.

units.zh: 是歲，侍郎錢徽所舉送，覆試多不中選，由是貶官，而舉人雜文復送中書門下。
units.en: That year most candidates presented by Vice-Minister Qian Hui failed the re-examination; he was demoted as a result, and candidates' literary compositions were once again forwarded to the Secretariat.
units.literal: That year, those presented by Vice-Minister Qian Hui largely failed the re-examination; he was demoted accordingly, and candidates' literary compositions were again sent to the Secretariat.

units.zh: 長慶三年，侍郎王起言：「故事，禮部已放榜，而中書門下始詳覆。
units.en: In 823, Vice-Minister Wang Qi said: "By precedent the Ministry of Rites posted examination results before the Secretariat conducted its detailed review.
units.literal: In the third year of Changqing, Vice-Minister Wang Qi said: "By precedent, the Ministry of Rites had already posted the list before the Secretariat began its detailed review.

units.zh: 今請先詳覆，而後放榜。」
units.en: I request that the Secretariat review candidates first and only then post the results."
units.literal: Now I request that detailed review come first, and posting the list afterward."

units.zh: 議者以起雖避嫌，然失貢職矣。
units.en: Critics replied that although Wang Qi was avoiding suspicion, he had neglected his proper duties as presenting officer.
units.literal: Critics held that although Wang Qi avoided suspicion, he had failed in his duty to present tribute scholars.

units.zh: 諫議大夫殷侑言：「《三史》為書，勸善懲惡，亞於《六經》。
units.en: Remonstrance officer Yin You said: "The Three Histories encourage virtue and condemn vice; they rank just below the Six Classics.
units.literal: Remonstrance Officer Yin You said: "The Three Histories as books encourage good and punish evil, ranking next to the Six Classics.

units.zh: 比來史學都廢，至有身處班列，而朝廷舊章莫能知者。」
units.en: Yet historical studies have been neglected until officials standing in court ranks no longer know the dynasty's own institutional precedents."
units.literal: In recent times historical studies have been wholly abandoned, so that there are men standing in court ranks who cannot know the old regulations of the court."

units.zh: 於是立史科及三傳科。
units.en: Thereupon the history examination and the Three Commentaries examination were established.
units.literal: Thereupon the history examination and the Three Commentaries examination were established.

units.zh: 大和三年，高鍇為考功員外郎，取士有不當，監察御史姚中立又奏停考功別頭試。
units.en: In 829, Gao Xi served as vice-director of the Directorate of Personnel and selected candidates improperly; investigating censor Yao Zhongli again memorialized to abolish the separate-head examination at the Directorate.
units.literal: In the third year of Dahe, Gao Xi was vice-director of the Directorate of Personnel; his selection of scholars was improper, and Investigating Censor Yao Zhongli again memorialized to suspend the Directorate's separate-head examination.

units.zh: 六年，侍郎賈餗又奏復之。
units.en: In 832, Vice-Minister Jia Su memorialized to restore it.
units.literal: In the sixth year, Vice-Minister Jia Su again memorialized to restore it.

units.zh: 八年，宰相王涯以為「禮部取士，乃先以榜示中書，非至公之道。
units.en: In 834, Chief Minister Wang Ya argued that "when the Ministry of Rites selects scholars, showing the results list to the Secretariat first is not the path of perfect fairness.
units.literal: In the eighth year, Chief Minister Wang Ya held that "when the Ministry of Rites selects scholars, it first shows the list to the Secretariat—this is not the way of utmost fairness.

units.zh: 自今一委有司，以所試雜文、鄉貫、三代名諱送中書門下」。
units.en: Henceforth the responsible offices alone should forward candidates' examination compositions, native-place records, and three generations of names and taboo names to the Secretariat."
units.literal: From now on let the responsible offices alone handle it, sending the literary compositions tested, native-place registers, and three generations of names and taboo names to the Secretariat."

units.zh: 大抵眾科之目，進士尤為貴，其得人亦最為盛焉。
units.en: Among all examination categories, the Jinshi degree was especially prized and produced the greatest number of outstanding men.
units.literal: Broadly speaking, among all examination categories, Jinshi was especially honored, and it produced the greatest number of worthy men.

units.zh: 方其取以辭章，類若浮文而少實；
units.en: When judged by literary composition alone, the degree seemed to reward flashy writing with little substance;
units.literal: When selection was by literary composition, it seemed mostly superficial writing with little substance;

units.zh: 及其臨事設施，奮其事業，隱然為國名臣者，不可勝數，遂使時君篤意，以謂莫此之尚。
units.en: yet when they took office and applied themselves, countless Jinshi graduates quietly became the state's most celebrated ministers—so that successive emperors devoted themselves to the degree, believing nothing surpassed it.
units.literal: yet when they took office and carried out affairs, striving in their careers, those who quietly became renowned ministers of state were beyond counting—so that rulers of the time devoted themselves to it, holding that nothing surpassed it.

units.zh: 及其後世，俗益媮薄，上下交疑，因以謂按其聲病，可以為有司之責，舍是則汗漫而無所守，遂不復能易。
units.en: In later generations customs grew lax and suspicious, and officials concluded that enforcing tonal and parallelism rules was responsibility enough; without them, standards dissolved entirely—so the system could no longer be reformed.
units.literal: In later generations customs grew laxer and meaner, suspicion ran between high and low, and it came to be held that judging tonal patterns could serve as the officials' responsibility; apart from this there was only unbounded license with nothing to hold to—so the system could no longer be changed.

units.zh: 嗚呼，乃知三代鄉里德行之舉，非至治之隆莫能行也。
units.en: Alas—thus one sees that the Three Dynasties' selection of men by village virtue and conduct could flourish only under the most perfect governance.
units.literal: Alas—thus one knows that the Three Dynasties' selection by village virtue and conduct could be practiced only under the height of perfect governance.

units.zh: 太宗時，冀州進士張昌齡、王公謹有名于當時，考功員外郎王師旦不署以第。
units.en: Under Taizong, Jinshi candidates Zhang Changling and Wang Gongjin of Jizhou were celebrated in their day, but Vice-Director Wang Shidan refused to pass them.
units.literal: Under Taizong, Jinshi candidates Zhang Changling and Wang Gongjin of Jizhou were famous in their day, but Vice-Director Wang Shidan would not sign them to a grade.

units.zh: 太宗問其故，對曰：「二人者，皆文采浮華，擢之將誘後生而弊風俗。」
units.en: Taizong asked why. He replied: "Both men write in a flashy, ornate style. Promoting them would mislead later students and corrupt public morals."
units.literal: Taizong asked the reason; he replied: "Both men's literary arts are flashy and ornate; promoting them would lure later students and harm custom."

units.zh: 其後，二人者卒不能有立。
units.en: In the end, neither man ever achieved lasting distinction.
units.literal: Afterward, neither of the two ever achieved lasting standing.

units.zh: 寶應二年，禮部侍郎楊綰上疏言：「進士科起于隋大業中，是時猶試策。
units.en: In 763, Vice-Minister Yang Wan submitted a memorial: "The Jinshi examination originated in the Sui Daye era, when candidates were still tested on policy questions.
units.literal: In the second year of Baoying, Vice-Minister of Rites Yang Wan submitted a memorial saying: "The Jinshi category arose in the Daye era of Sui; at that time policy questions were still tested.

units.zh: 高宗朝，劉思立加進士雜文，明經填帖，故為進士者皆誦當代之文，而不通經史，明經者但記帖括。
units.en: Under Gaozong, Liu Sili added literary compositions to the Jinshi examination and fill-in passages to Mingjing; Jinshi candidates thereafter memorized contemporary essays without mastering the classics or histories, while Mingjing candidates merely memorized passage extracts.
units.literal: In the Gaozong reign, Liu Sili added literary compositions for Jinshi and fill-in passages for Mingjing; thus Jinshi candidates all recited contemporary writings without mastering classics and histories, while Mingjing candidates merely memorized passage extracts.

units.zh: 又投牒自舉，非古先哲王側席待賢之道。
units.en: Candidates also submit their own credentials—unlike the ancient sage-kings who cleared their seats to await worthy men.
units.literal: Moreover they submit credentials and recommend themselves—this is not the way of ancient sage-kings who vacated their seats to await the worthy.

units.zh: 請依古察孝廉，其鄉閭孝友、信義、廉恥而通經者，縣薦之州，州試其所通之學，送於省。
units.en: I propose reviving the ancient investigation of Filial and Incorrupt men: those known in their villages for filial piety, friendship, faithfulness, righteousness, integrity, and shame at wrongdoing who have mastered the classics should be recommended by the county to the prefecture, tested on their learning by the prefecture, and sent to the capital.
units.literal: I request following antiquity in investigating Filial and Incorrupt candidates: those in their villages who were filial, friendly, faithful, righteous, honest, and ashamed of wrongdoing and who had mastered the classics—the county should recommend them to the prefecture, the prefecture should test the learning they had mastered, and send them to the capital.

units.zh: 自縣至省，皆勿自投牒，其到狀、保辨、識牒皆停。
units.en: From county to capital, candidates should not submit credentials on their own; arrival documents, guarantor verification, and identification papers should all be abolished.
units.literal: From county to capital, none should submit credentials on their own; arrival documents, guarantor verification, and identification papers should all be discontinued.

units.zh: 而所習經，取大義，聽通諸家之學。
units.en: Examinations should test broad mastery of the classics' meaning and permit knowledge drawn from all scholarly traditions.
units.literal: For the classics studied, take the great principles and permit mastery of learning from all schools.

units.zh: 每問經十條，對策三道，皆通，為上第，吏部官之；
units.en: Ten questions on the classics and three policy responses—passing all earned top grade and appointment by the Ministry of Personnel;
units.literal: Ten classic questions each session, three policy responses—if all passed, this was the top grade and the Ministry of Personnel appointed them to office;

units.zh: 經義通八，策通二，為中第，與出身；
units.en: passing eight classic questions and two policy questions earned middle grade and initial qualification;
units.literal: passing eight on classic meaning and two on policy was middle grade, granting initial qualification;

units.zh: 下第，罷歸。
units.en: failure meant dismissal and return home.
units.literal: lower grade meant dismissal and return home.

units.zh: 《論語》、《孝經》、《孟子》兼為一經，其明經、進士及道舉並停。」
units.en: The Analects, Classic of Filial Piety, and Mencius together would count as one classic; the Mingjing, Jinshi, and Daoist recommendation examinations should all be abolished."
units.literal: The Analects, Classic of Filial Piety, and Mencius together counted as one classic; the Mingjing, Jinshi, and Daoist recommendation examinations should all be suspended."

units.zh: 詔給事中李棲筠、李廙、尚書左丞賈至、京兆尹兼御史大夫嚴武議。
units.en: The emperor ordered palace attendants Li Qiyun and Li Yi, left assistant minister Jia Zhi, and Jingzhao intendant and concurrent censor-in-chief Yan Wu to deliberate.
units.literal: An edict ordered Palace Attendants Li Qiyun and Li Yi, Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs Jia Zhi, and Jingzhao Intendant and concurrent Censor-in-Chief Yan Wu to deliberate.

units.zh: 棲筠等議曰：
units.en: Li Qiyun and the others replied:
units.literal: Li Qiyun and the others deliberated, saying:

units.zh: 「夏之政忠，商之政敬，周之政文，然則文與忠敬皆統人行。
units.en: "Xia government was marked by sincerity, Shang by reverence, Zhou by culture—yet culture, sincerity, and reverence alike govern human conduct.
units.literal: "The government of Xia was marked by sincerity, that of Shang by reverence, that of Zhou by culture—thus culture together with sincerity and reverence all govern human conduct.

units.zh: 且諡號述行，莫美于文，文興則忠敬存焉。
units.en: Posthumous titles describe a person's conduct, and none is finer than "Cultured"; when culture flourishes, sincerity and reverence endure.
units.literal: Moreover, posthumous titles describe conduct, and none is more beautiful than culture; when culture flourishes, sincerity and reverence are preserved therein.

units.zh: 故前代以文取士，本文行也，由辭觀行，則及辭焉。
units.en: Earlier dynasties selected officials by literary accomplishment because writing reveals character; to judge conduct through writing is to reach the writing itself.
units.literal: Therefore earlier ages took scholars by literary accomplishment—this was rooted in conduct and character; observing conduct through literary expression reaches even to the expression itself.

units.zh: 宣父稱顏子「不遷怒，不貳過」，謂之「好學」。
units.en: Confucius praised Yan Hui for "never transferring anger, never repeating a fault," and called this true love of learning.
units.literal: The Master praised Yan Hui for "not transferring anger, not repeating faults," calling this "fondness for learning."

units.zh: 今試學者以帖字為精通，不窮旨義，豈能知遷怒、貳過之道乎？
units.en: Today we test students on fill-in passages as if that were mastery, without probing deeper meaning—how can they grasp the way of not transferring anger or repeating faults?
units.literal: Today examinees are tested on fill-in characters as mastery, without exhausting principles and meanings—how can they know the way of not transferring anger or repeating faults?

units.zh: 考文者以聲病為是非，豈能知移風易俗化天下乎？
units.en: Examiners judge compositions by tonal patterns—how can they know how to transform customs and civilize the realm?
units.literal: Those who examine literary works take tonal patterns as the standard of right and wrong—how can they know transforming customs and changing popular ways to civilize all under Heaven?

units.zh: 是以上失其源，下襲其流，先王之道莫能行也。
units.en: Thus those above have lost the source and those below merely follow the current—the way of the ancient kings can no longer be practiced.
units.literal: Thus above loses the source and below inherits the current; the way of the former kings can no longer be practiced.

units.zh: 夫先王之道消，則小人之道長，亂臣賊子由是生焉！
units.en: When the way of the ancient kings fades, the way of petty men flourishes—and rebellious ministers and wicked sons arise from it!
units.literal: When the way of the former kings fades, the way of petty men grows long—rebellious ministers and wicked sons arise from this!

units.zh: 今取士試之小道，而不以遠大，是猶以蝸蚓之餌垂海，而望吞舟之魚，不亦難乎？
units.en: To select officials by petty tests rather than great purpose is like dangling worm bait over the sea and hoping to catch a leviathan—is it not futile?
units.literal: Now in taking scholars one tests petty paths and not the far-reaching and great—this is like dangling snail-and-worm bait over the sea and hoping for fish that swallow boats—is it not difficult?

units.zh: 所以食垂餌者皆小魚，就科目者皆小藝。
units.en: Only small fish take dangling bait; only petty skills win examination degrees.
units.literal: Those that eat dangling bait are all small fish; those who pursue examination categories are all petty arts.

units.zh: 且夏有天下四百載，禹之道喪而商始興；
units.en: Xia ruled for four hundred years before Yu's way was lost and Shang rose;
units.literal: Moreover, Xia held the realm for four hundred years; Yu's way was lost and Shang then rose;

units.zh: 商有天下六百祀，湯之法棄而周始興；
units.en: Shang ruled for six hundred years before Tang's laws were abandoned and Zhou rose;
units.literal: Shang held the realm for six hundred reign-years; Tang's laws were abandoned and Zhou then rose;

units.zh: 周有天下八百年，文、武之政廢而秦始並焉。
units.en: Zhou ruled for eight hundred years before the government of King Wen and King Wu was abandoned and Qin united the realm.
units.literal: Zhou held the realm for eight hundred years; the government of Wen and Wu was abandoned and Qin then united it.

units.zh: 三代之選士任賢，皆考實行，是以風俗淳一，運祚長遠。
units.en: The Three Dynasties selected officials by examining actual conduct; customs remained pure and their rule endured.
units.literal: The Three Dynasties in selecting scholars and appointing the worthy all examined actual conduct; thus customs were pure and unified and fortune endured far and long.

units.zh: 漢興，監其然，尊儒術，尚名節，雖近戚竊位，強臣擅權，弱主外立，母后專政，而亦能終彼四百，豈非學行之效邪？
units.en: When Han arose, it observed this pattern, honored Confucian learning, and prized integrity. Though kinsmen seized office, powerful ministers monopolized authority, weak rulers were installed from outside, and empress dowagers dominated government, Han still endured four hundred years—is this not the fruit of learning and conduct?
units.literal: When Han arose, it observed this, honored Confucian learning, and esteemed reputation and integrity; though close kin usurped posts, powerful ministers monopolized authority, weak rulers were installed from outside, and empress dowagers held government—yet it could still complete those four hundred years—is this not the effect of learning and conduct?

units.zh: 魏、晉以來，專尚浮侈，德義不修，故子孫速顛，享國不永也。
units.en: From Wei and Jin onward, rulers prized superficial luxury and neglected virtue and righteousness; their dynasties fell swiftly and did not endure.
units.literal: From Wei and Jin onward, they devoted themselves only to superficial luxury and did not cultivate virtue and righteousness; thus their descendants quickly fell and their enjoyment of the realm was not long.

units.zh: 今綰所請，實為正論。
units.en: Yang Wan's proposal is fundamentally sound.
units.literal: What Wan now requests is truly correct doctrine.

units.zh: 然自晉室之亂，南北分裂，人多僑處，必欲復古鄉舉裏選，竊恐未盡。
units.en: Yet since the Jin collapse and the north-south division, many people have lived far from their native places; a full restoration of ancient village recommendation and district selection may not yet be practicable.
units.literal: Yet since the disorder of the Jin house, north and south were divided and many people lived as sojourners; if one must restore the ancient village recommendation and district selection, I fear privately that it may not be fully feasible.

units.zh: 請兼廣學校，以明訓誘。
units.en: I propose instead expanding the schools to spread instruction and moral guidance.
units.literal: I request also expanding the schools to make instruction clear and guide by teaching.

units.zh: 雖京師州縣皆有小學，兵革之後，生徒流離，儒臣、師氏，祿廩無向。
units.en: Although the capital and prefectures all maintained elementary schools, after the wars students scattered and Confucian teachers had no reliable salaries.
units.literal: Although the capital and prefectures and counties all had elementary schools, after the armies and weapons, student disciples were scattered, Confucian officials and teachers had no direction for salary and grain rations.

units.zh: 請增博士員，厚其稟稍，選通儒碩生，間居其職。
units.en: Increase the number of erudites, raise their stipends, and appoint broadly learned eminent scholars to these posts.
units.literal: I request increasing the number of erudites, enriching their stipends, and selecting broadly learned eminent scholars to fill the posts in turn.

units.zh: 十道大郡，置太學館，遣博士出外，兼領郡官，以教生徒。
units.en: In the major prefectures of the ten circuits, establish Imperial University hostels, dispatch erudites to serve concurrently as prefectural officials, and charge them with instructing students.
units.literal: In the great prefectures of the ten circuits, establish Imperial University hostels, send erudites outward, and have them concurrently hold prefectural office to instruct student disciples.

units.zh: 保桑梓者，鄉里舉焉；
units.en: Those who remain in their native districts should be recommended by village and township;
units.literal: Those who preserve their native place should be recommended by village and district;

units.zh: 在流寓者，庠序推焉。
units.en: those living abroad should be nominated by local schools.
units.literal: those living as sojourners should be promoted by the local schools.

units.zh: 朝而行之，夕見其利。」
units.en: Adopt this in the morning and see its benefit by evening."
units.literal: Implement it in the morning and by evening see its benefit."

units.zh: 而大臣以為舉人循習，難於速變，請自來歲始。
units.en: The chief ministers argued that candidates were accustomed to the existing system and rapid change would be difficult; they asked that reform begin the following year.
units.literal: But the great ministers held that candidates were accustomed to established practice and rapid change would be difficult; they requested beginning from the coming year.

units.zh: 帝以問翰林學士，對曰：「舉進士久矣，廢之恐失其業。」
units.en: The emperor consulted Hanlin academicians, who replied: "Candidates have pursued the Jinshi degree for generations; abolishing it overnight would destroy their livelihoods."
units.literal: The emperor questioned Hanlin Academicians; they replied: "Taking the Jinshi examination has been long established; abolishing it would fear losing their livelihood."

units.zh: 乃詔明經、進士與孝廉兼行。
units.en: An edict was issued ordering Mingjing, Jinshi, and Filial and Incorrupt examinations to continue side by side.
units.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered Mingjing, Jinshi, and Filial and Incorrupt to be practiced together.

units.zh: 先是，進士試詩、賦及時務策五道，明經策三道。
units.en: Previously, Jinshi candidates were tested on poetry, rhapsody, and five current-affairs policy questions; Mingjing candidates on three policy questions.
units.literal: Earlier, Jinshi were tested on poetry, rhapsody, and five current-affairs policy questions; Mingjing on three policy questions.

units.zh: 建中二年，中書舍人趙贊權知貢舉，乃以箴、論、表、贊代詩、賦，而皆試策三道。
units.en: In 781, acting examination supervisor Zhao Zan replaced poetry and rhapsody with admonitions, discourses, memorials, and eulogies, and required all candidates to answer three policy questions.
units.literal: In the second year of Jianzhong, Secretariat Drafter Zhao Zan acted as supervisor of tribute presentation; he replaced poetry and rhapsody with admonitions, discourses, memorials, and eulogies, and all were tested on three policy questions.

units.zh: 大和八年，禮部復罷進士議論，而試詩、賦。
units.en: In 834, the Ministry of Rites again abolished Jinshi discursive essays and restored poetry and rhapsody examinations.
units.literal: In the eighth year of Dahe, the Ministry of Rites again abolished Jinshi discursive essays and tested poetry and rhapsody.

units.zh: 文宗從內出題以試進士，謂侍臣曰：「吾患文格浮薄，昨自出題，所試差勝。」
units.en: Emperor Wenzong set the examination topics himself and told his ministers: "I worry that literary standards have grown shallow; the compositions from yesterday's examination, for which I set the topics myself, were somewhat better."
units.literal: Wenzong issued the topics from within the palace to test Jinshi candidates and said to attending ministers: "I worry that literary standards are superficial and thin; yesterday I set the topics myself, and those tested were somewhat better."

units.zh: 乃詔禮部歲取登第者三十人，苟無其人，不必充其數。
units.en: He ordered the Ministry of Rites to pass thirty candidates each year—but not to fill the quota if no worthy candidates were found.
units.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered the Ministry of Rites to take thirty who passed each year; if there were no such men, it was not necessary to fill the quota.

units.zh: 是時，文宗好學嗜古，鄭覃以經術位宰相，深嫉進士浮薄，屢請罷之。
units.en: Wenzong loved learning and antiquity; Zheng Tan, a classicist who had risen to chief minister, deeply resented the Jinshi degree's superficiality and repeatedly petitioned to abolish it.
units.literal: At that time Wenzong loved learning and cherished antiquity; Zheng Tan, by classical learning, held the post of chief minister and deeply resented the superficiality of Jinshi candidates, repeatedly requesting their abolition.

units.zh: 文宗曰：「敦厚浮薄，色色有之，進士科取人二百年矣，不可遽廢。」
units.en: Wenzong replied: "Solid worth and superficiality exist in every walk of life. The Jinshi examination has selected officials for two hundred years—it cannot be abolished overnight."
units.literal: Wenzong said: "Solid worth and superficiality exist in every kind; the Jinshi category has selected men for two hundred years—it cannot be abruptly abolished."

units.zh: 因得不罷。
units.en: The degree was therefore preserved.
units.literal: Thus it was not abolished.

units.zh: 武宗即位，宰相李德裕尤惡進士。
units.en: When Wuzong ascended the throne, Chief Minister Li Deyu especially despised Jinshi degree-holders.
units.literal: When Wuzong took the throne, Chief Minister Li Deyu especially detested Jinshi candidates.

units.zh: 初，舉人既及第，綴行通名，詣主司第謝。
units.en: After passing the examination, candidates would line up in procession, announce their names, and visit the chief examiner's residence to give thanks.
units.literal: Initially, after candidates had passed, they lined up in procession announcing their names and went to the examiner's residence to give thanks.

units.zh: 其制，序立西階下，北上東向；
units.en: By regulation they formed ranks below the western steps, proceeding northward and facing east;
units.literal: The procedure: they arranged themselves in order below the western steps, proceeding north and facing east;

units.zh: 主人席東階下。
units.en: the examiner was seated below the eastern steps.
units.literal: the host was seated below the eastern steps.

units.zh: 西向；
units.en: facing west;
units.literal: Facing west;

units.zh: 諸生拜，主司答拜；
units.en: the candidates bowed and the examiner returned the bow;
units.literal: the students bowed and the examiner returned the bow;

units.zh: 乃敘齒，謝恩，遂升階，與公卿觀者皆坐；
units.en: then, in order of seniority, they expressed their gratitude, ascended the steps, and sat with the observing officials;
units.literal: then by seniority they thanked him for the favor, ascended the steps, and all sat together with the observing dukes and ministers;

units.zh: 酒數行，乃赴期集。
units.en: after several rounds of wine they proceeded to the scheduled banquet.
units.literal: after several rounds of wine they went on to the scheduled gathering.

units.zh: 又有曲江會、題名席。
units.en: There were also the Qujiang gathering and the inscription banquet.
units.literal: There were also the Qujiang gathering and the inscription banquet.

units.zh: 至是，德裕奏：「國家設科取士，而附黨背公，自為門生。
units.en: At this point Li Deyu memorialized: "The state established examinations to select officials, yet candidates form factions, betray the public interest, and style themselves the examiner's personal disciples.
units.literal: At this point De Yu memorialized: "The state established examination categories to take scholars, yet they attach to factions, betray the public good, and make themselves the examiner's disciples.

units.zh: 自今一見有司而止，其期集、參謁、曲江題名皆罷。」
units.en: Henceforth candidates would pay their respects to the examining officials once and no more; the scheduled gatherings, courtesy visits, and Qujiang inscription banquets were all abolished."
units.literal: From now on they should see the offices once and stop; the scheduled gatherings, courtesy calls, and Qujiang inscription banquets were all abolished."

units.zh: 德裕嘗論公卿子弟艱于科舉，武宗曰：「向聞楊虞卿兄弟朋比貴勢，妨平進之路。
units.en: Li Deyu once argued that sons of high ministers struggled in the civil examinations. Wuzong replied: "I have heard that the Yang Yuqing brothers formed factions with the powerful and blocked the path of fair advancement.
units.literal: Li Deyu once discussed how sons of high ministers found the civil examinations difficult; Wuzong said: "I have heard that the brothers Yang Yuqing formed factions with the powerful and blocked the path of fair advancement.

units.zh: 昨黜楊知至、鄭樸等，抑其太甚耳。
units.en: When I demoted Yang Zhizhi, Zheng Pu, and the others yesterday, I was only reining in excesses that had gone too far.
units.literal: Yesterday Yang Zhizhi, Zheng Pu, and others were demoted—that was merely restraining them too harshly.

units.zh: 有司不識朕意，不放子弟，即過矣，但取實藝可也。」
units.en: The examining officials failed to grasp my meaning. Refusing to admit officials' sons would itself be excessive; they need only select candidates with genuine ability."
units.literal: The offices did not understand my intent; not to admit sons of officials would be going too far—they need only select those with real ability."

units.zh: 德裕曰：「鄭肅、封敖子弟皆有才，不敢應舉。
units.en: Li Deyu said: "The sons of Zheng Su and Feng Ao are all talented, yet they dare not sit for the examinations.
units.literal: Li Deyu said: "The sons of Zheng Su and Feng Ao all have talent but dare not enter the examinations.

units.zh: 臣無名第，不當非進士。
units.en: I hold no examination degree myself and should not disparage the Jinshi examination.
units.literal: Your servant has no examination degree and ought not to disparage Jinshi.

units.zh: 然臣祖天寶末以仕進無他岐，勉強隨計，一舉登第。
units.en: Yet my grandfather, at the end of the Tianbao era, had no other path to office and reluctantly sat for the examinations, passing on his first attempt.
